title: MOSFET: switch and square-law transfer
goal: Use a 2N7000 as a logic-driven switch for an LED, then measure its drain current against gate voltage and compare with the square law.
theory: An enhancement N-MOSFET is off until the gate–source voltage passes the threshold V_th (about 2 V here). The gate draws no DC current, so a logic output can drive it directly.
Fully on (V_GS well above V_th, small V_DS) the channel acts like a small resistor R_DS(on) ≈ 1/(k·(V_GS − V_th)); a switch should leave only millivolts across it.
In saturation (V_DS > V_GS − V_th) the drain current follows the square law I_D = (k/2)·(V_GS − V_th)²·(1 + λ·V_DS). The simulator's 2N7000 has k = 0.1 A/V², V_th = 2 V and λ = 0.01 /V.

prelab.label: I_D in saturation at V_GS = 3 V (ignore λ)
Drain voltage with R_D = 100 Ω from 12 V

procedure: Load the reference build. Flip the logic switch LS1 (click it, or its Properties): the LED follows. Measure V_DS of Q1 while on.
The trimmer TR sets Q2's gate. M2 reads V_GS, M1 the drain. At V_GS = 3 V compare I_D = (12 − V_D)/100 Ω with the square law.
Turn TR in small steps from 2 V to 3.5 V and note I_D: it grows with the square of the overdrive.
On the curve tracer (mode nmos) trace Q3: one curve per gate voltage; find the knee where V_DS = V_GS − V_th.
